title: THE WINTER WAR: How Finland Survived Stalin's Invasion (1939–1940)
editorial_promise: An evidence-led account of how Finland resisted the Soviet invasion, how Soviet forces adapted, and why the 1940 peace preserved Finnish independence at the cost of territory.
historical_scope: 30 November 1939 to 13 March 1940, with limited pre-war context
key_accuracy_constraints: Finland survived as an independent state; do not say it defeated the Soviet Union.
The Mannerheim Line was not a continuous concrete wall.
Motti tactics were situational and not universally successful.
Soviet forces adapted and broke through in February 1940.
Treaty signed 12 March 1940; fighting ceased 13 March 1940.
Avoid unsupported precise casualty or displacement totals.
